figures.alt: Historic wood window sill under careful repair with sound retained material, matching wood pieces, and protected surrounding trim
figures.caption: Historic review often turns on whether work preserves the visible character and material logic of the building. Repair, compatible replacement, details, proportions, and documentation matter at the street-facing elements.

figures.alt: Historic masonry restoration with carefully opened access area, retained original wall, matching repair materials, and protected work zone
figures.caption: Historic structural work needs investigation before intervention. Existing materials, movement, water, earlier alterations, load paths, access, repair compatibility, and the work needed to protect adjacent fabric all shape the solution.

figures.alt: Commercial interior rough-in with coordinated HVAC ductwork, sprinkler mains, conduit racks, cable tray, piping, and support systems before drywall
figures.caption: Modern systems have to be brought into an old building without treating the historic structure as empty space. Routes, clearances, access, ventilation, drainage, fire protection, electrical work, and finish restoration need to be coordinated.
